eligibility_rubric: survives the complete C1 base suite and the direct revalidation run
the changed behavior conflicts with a specific public C1 specification requirement
the behavior is observable through the documented command-line interface
a deterministic input can distinguish C1 from the mutant
the required inputs are present in the pinned task data or can be constructed with the supplied task fixture
the mutant is not equivalent or unreachable for the chosen valid input
sampling_unit: one representative mutant per distinct specification-level behavior family; include the full eligible representative pool when it is at most 20

mutants.specification_basis: The specification requires unique parameter names. Removing the duplicate-key hook accepts a JSON object with repeated root keys, which is externally visible in CLI success/output versus the required schema failure.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A small deterministic schema JSON file containing the same parameter key twice is sufficient; no environment or external fixture is required.

mutants.specification_basis: The rule schema requires id to be a non-empty string. The mutation can accept a non-string, truthy identifier.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A deterministic JSON rule with a numeric nonzero id distinguishes the behavior through CLI rejection and stdout/stderr.

mutants.specification_basis: The rules-array constraints require id values to be unique. The mutation stops recording each actual ID and can accept a duplicate.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A deterministic rules JSON array with two otherwise valid rules sharing one id is sufficient.

mutants.specification_basis: The rule schema requires a non-empty pattern string. The mutation can accept an empty string.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A deterministic rule with pattern set to an empty string is sufficient.

mutants.specification_basis: When languages is present, it may contain only the string python. The mutation ignores the specified languages field and can accept an unsupported language value.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A deterministic valid-shape rule with languages set to ["javascript"] distinguishes acceptance from required rejection. Mutants 58 and 59 are redundant variants of the same behavior family and are not sampled separately.

mutants.specification_basis: The specification independently requires languages to be an array of strings and limits every value to python. The mutation weakens the combined validation and can admit an unsupported language.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A deterministic languages array containing an unsupported string is sufficient.

mutants.specification_basis: The regex_flags array may contain any subset of i, m, and s; multiple listed flags must all affect regex matching. The mutation overwrites rather than combines the flags.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A deterministic multiline, case-insensitive regex input requiring both m and i distinguishes the result.

mutants.specification_basis: The rule schema states regex_flags are only valid for kind=regex. The mutation can ignore that field when kind=exact.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A deterministic exact-match rule that also supplies regex_flags must be rejected. Mutant 103 is a redundant key-name variant of this same specification-level behavior family.

mutants.specification_basis: Output line coordinates are explicitly 1-based. The mutation can miscount a match following a newline at offset zero.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A source file beginning with a newline followed by a matching character yields a deterministic expected line number.

mutants.specification_basis: Output column coordinates are explicitly 1-based. The mutation can miscount a match following a newline at offset zero.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: A source file beginning with a newline followed by a matching character yields a deterministic expected column number.

mutants.specification_basis: The SDE contract says only items with published==1 are valid. The mutation admits a recipe whose blueprint is unpublished even when a published recipe is available for that product.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: The pinned SDE contains a published product with both an unpublished and a published blueprint recipe; the IDs and recipe data can be discovered from the supplied SDE fixture.

mutants.specification_basis: The canonical output requires Market Group: None when no market group exists. The mutation forces the market-path branch for an item with an empty market path.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: The pinned SDE includes published recipe items without market groups; a test can deterministically select one from the SDE tables.

mutants.specification_basis: The canonical output requires the literal None for an item without a market group. The mutation changes that literal.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: The pinned SDE includes published recipe items without market groups. Mutant 423 is a redundant alternate spelling in the same behavior family and is not sampled separately.

mutants.specification_basis: The output volume must be the item's SDE volume, while only ship items use packaged ship volume. The mutation formats non-ship volume as if it were a ship and can change its numeric value.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: The pinned SDE and visible examples include non-ship items with more than two decimal places in their volume.

mutants.specification_basis: The canonical block requires the exact Recipe: heading and ordering. The mutation removes the required heading/newline.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: Any valid published recipe in the supplied SDE provides a deterministic CLI oracle. Mutants 430 and 431 are redundant heading-format variants and are not sampled separately.

mutants.specification_basis: The materials table must be sorted alphabetically by item name case-insensitively. The mutation changes the ordering rule.
mutants.trigger_feasibility: The pinned SDE contains a published recipe whose material names distinguish case-insensitive from case-sensitive ordering.

redundant_behavior_variants.rationale: Same public behavior family: ignores the supplied languages key and may accept unsupported languages.
Same public behavior family: ignores the supplied languages key and may accept unsupported languages.
Same public behavior family: ignores regex_flags on exact rules.
Same public requirement and trigger: the no-market-group literal is incorrect.
Same public requirement and trigger: the canonical Recipe heading is incorrect.
Same public requirement and trigger: the canonical Recipe heading is incorrect.

excluded_mutant_families.rationale: The decode-error continue-to-break behavior depends on filesystem enumeration order; deterministic ordering is not guaranteed by the public contract.
The exact-match overlap behavior is not specified, so an assertion about overlapping matches would not have a specification-backed oracle.
The pinned SDE has no published recipe product with zero volume; a custom SDE fixture would be required, so this target is excluded from the initial controlled sample.
